title: § 164.308 Administrative safeguards

reasoning: The system does implement recording of some activities (transaction log, login success/failure), but it does not cover all activity involving PHI. title: § 164.308 Administrative safeguards

title: § 164.308 Administrative safeguards

reasoning: The only mitigations are requiring a CAPTCHA after three failed logins from an IP and blocking further password resets with “Too many retries” after three failed reset attempts from an IP which are not enough for all security incidents.

title: § 164.312 Technical safeguards

So access is further restricted by role and URL path in web.xml. (3) ePHI is not only “by role” but also “this user can only see this patient’s data.” For example, in ViewMyRecordsAction, the code uses the user’s ID so they only get their own record.

title: § 164.508 Uses and disclosures for which an authorization is required
description: The system shall require that a valid authorization for use or disclosure of protected health information contain at least the following elements: (i) A description of the information to be used or disclosed that identifies the information in a specific and meaningful fashion. (iii) The name or other specific identification of the person(s), or class of persons, to whom the covered entity may make the requested use or disclosure. (iv) A description of each purpose of the requested use or disclosure. The statement “at the request of the individual” is a sufficient description of the purpose when an individual initiates the authorization and does not, or elects not to, provide a statement of the purpose. (v) An expiration date or an expiration event that relates to the individual or the purpose of the use or disclosure. The statement “end of the research study,” “none,” or similar language is sufficient if the authorization is for a use or disclosure of protected health information for research, including for the creation and maintenance of a research database or research repository. reasoning: The authorization contains a generic text and multiple mandatory elements ((ii), (iv), (v), and part of (vi)) are missing.

title: § 164.308 Administrative safeguards
description: The system shall implement procedures for guarding against malicious software.
reasoning: The system has no malware-specific safeguards (no antivirus, no file scanning). It implements procedures that reduce the impact of malicious input, which can be considered partial “guarding” against malicious behavior. (1) Many JSPs use StringEscapeUtils.escapeHtml() when outputting user input to help guard against script injection in the browser. However, it is not enforced across the entire codebase. For example, Review text is user-generated, and output without escaping is a direct XSS risk.  Also, appointment comments are stored and displayed without escaping. (2) DAOs use PreparedStatement for database access, so user input is parameterized and not concatenated into SQL, reducing SQL injection risk. (3) Validators and ValidationFormat reject invalid input. (4) The only upload (patient CSV) is parsed as CSV, so the app does not blindly accept arbitrary files.

title: § 164.306 Security standards: General rules
description: The system shall protect against any reasonably anticipated threats or hazards to the security of electronic protected health information (ePHI).
reasoning: The system protects against any reasonably anticipated threats or hazards to the security of ePHI by (1) Many JSPs use StringEscapeUtils.escapeHtml() when outputting user input to help guard against script injection in the browser. However, it is not enforced across the entire codebase. For example, Review text is user-generated, and output without escaping is a direct XSS risk.  Also, appointment comments are stored and displayed without escaping. (2) DAOs use PreparedStatement for database access, so user input is parameterized and not concatenated into SQL, reducing SQL injection risk. (3) Validators and ValidationFormat reject invalid input. (4) The only upload (patient CSV) is parsed as CSV, so the app does not blindly accept arbitrary files.

title: § 164.308 Administrative safeguards
description: The system shall support the organization in implementing policies and procedures to prevent security violations.
reasoning: The system supports prevention of security violations through: (1) Role-based access control via web.xml restricts ePHI access to authorized roles only. (2) Password safeguarding uses salted SHA-256 hashing (AuthDAO). (3) CAPTCHA is triggered after three failed login attempts, and password reset is blocked after three failed attempts. (4) PreparedStatements in DAOs prevent SQL injection. (5) Many JSPs use StringEscapeUtils.escapeHtml() to guard against XSS, though this is not consistently applied across the codebase (e.g., review text is stored and displayed without escaping). However, the system lacks encryption of stored ePHI.
